extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of political and natural philosophy; clergy, scholars, and statesmen interested in Hobbes' critique of scholastic and religious doctrines
extracted.subtask_description: A chapter-length philosophical critique (Hobbes' Leviathan) diagnosing errors introduced into religion, natural philosophy, and civil polity by vain scholastic reasoning and fabulous traditions. The text lays out a working definition of 'philosophy', diagnoses common mistaken doctrines (metaphysical, physical, moral), and gives examples of their pernicious effects on religion and government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: By Philosophy is understood 'the Knowledge acquired by Reasoning, from the Manner of the Generation of any thing, to the Properties; or from the Properties, to some possible Way of Generation of the same; to the end to bee able to produce, as far as matter, and humane force permit, such Effects, as humane life requireth.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: the Geometrician reasons from construction to properties (and back) to measure land; the Astronomer reasons from motions of heavenly bodies to causes of seasons and time. Philosophy is knowledge gained by right reasoning about causes and effects, aimed at producing useful results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prudence is not Philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: Prudence (original knowledge called Experience) is not part of philosophy because it is not attained by reasoning but is a memory of successions of events; it can be found in brute beasts as well as men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes empirical, experience-based judgement (prudence) from deductive, general, eternal truths produced by reasoning; warns that prudence is contingent and easily frustrated by small changes in circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: False doctrine cannot be philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: Any false conclusions do not count as philosophy: 'For he that Reasoneth aright in words he understandeth, can never conclude an Error.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philosophy, if genuine, yields true conclusions by right reasoning; therefore doctrines known to be false should not be called philosophy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revelation is not part of Philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowledge acquired by supernatural revelation is not philosophy because it is not obtained by reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separates theological revelation from philosophical knowledge; revelation is a different category and should not be conflated with reasoned explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority-based learning is not philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: Learning taken upon the credit of authors (reasoning from authority) is not true philosophy but faith, because it is not reasoning from cause to effect or effect to cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warns against treating Aristotle's texts (or any authoritative corpus) as equivalent to reasoned philosophy; stresses independent causal reasoning over deference to authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leisure and commonwealth as prerequisites for philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: Leasure is the mother of Philosophy; Common-wealth (peace and extended polities) produces the leisure necessary for the study and method of philosophy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical/examples: flourishing cities with peace produced philosophical schools (Gymnosophists, Magi). Lack of leisure due to subsistence and war prevents systematic philosophical inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophy must be grounded in method and demonstrative sciences
rubrics_metrics.description: True natural philosophy requires method (logic grounded in geometry and demonstrative sciences) rather than mere disputation and rhetorical prating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plato excluded those not versed in geometry; Hobbes criticizes Athenian schools for idle disputing and the schools’ tendency to produce senseless language and no rigorous method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid turning law/theology into mere scholastic disputation
rubrics_metrics.description: Schools (including Jewish synagogues turned schools) that read and dispute law often corrupted texts with false commentaries and vain traditions, turning doctrine into phantastical philosophy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Jewish Lectures and Disputations corrupted the Law and led to misunderstanding of the Prophets; warns against mixing scholastic disputation and religious texts to produce unfounded doctrines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universities should not substitute Aristotelian authority for true philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: An university that makes Aristotle's authority the standard produces 'Aristotelity' not real philosophy; geometry and rigour have often been absent from such institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical note: universities incorporated public schools and subordinated philosophy to Roman religion and law; caution against institutional capture of thought by one author or tradition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject metaphysical doctrine of abstract/separated essences
rubrics_metrics.description: The notion of 'Abstract Essences' or 'Substantiall Formes' separated from bodies is false and leads to absurdities (e.g., souls wholly present in every body-part, essences existing where there is no body).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains linguistic origin of such terms and shows how they produce paradoxes (souls everywhere, faith/virtue 'poured in' or 'blown into' men), weakening subjects’ dependence on sovereign power and enabling priestly pretensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid non-physical incorporeal explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: Asserting incorporeal substances without dimensions (incorporeal souls/essences) produces insoluble problems about place, motion, and sensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: how can incorporeal souls feel pain, be tormented by fire, or 'go' to Heaven/Purgatory? Such claims rely on empty distinctions ('definitive' vs 'circumscriptive') and are mere words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not define eternity as a mere 'nunc-stans' (standing of present)
rubrics_metrics.description: The scholastic definition of Eternity as 'the Standing still of the Present Time' (Nunc-stans) is unintelligible and used to avoid problems about God's will and foreknowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hobbes calls this a school jargon (Nunc-stans) and compares it to the equally meaningless 'Hic-stans' for infinite place; warns against resorting to unintelligible metaphors for divine attributes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject claims of ubiquity for bodies and spirits
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims that a body may be in many places at once, or many bodies in one place simultaneously (e.g., corporeal ubiquity) are incongruous and logically incoherent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows how dividing bodies implies dividing places; ubiquity doctrines arise from confusing mental subdivisions with physical place and from scholastic abuse of terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Causes must not be circular (critique of 'heaviness' as cause of falling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explaining natural phenomena by tautological or circular terms (e.g., calling things heavy and defining heaviness as an endeavour to go to the center of the earth) is vacuous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hobbes exposes such scholastic physics where definitions merely restate the phenomenon; urges causal explanations that genuinely account for mechanism rather than rename effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject notion of putting quantity into an already-made body
rubrics_metrics.description: The scholastic idea that a body becomes larger by having 'quantity put into it' (condensed/rarefied) is incoherent, since quantity is the determination of matter itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues that quantity cannot be added to a pre-existing body as if body were previously quantity-less; such language betrays conceptual confusion about matter and magnitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject vague explanations like 'pouring in of souls' and ubiquity of species
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanations such as 'Creatur Infundendo' (souls created by pouring in) and 'ubiquity of species' for sense are idle phrases that don't explain causal mechanism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labels these scholastic locutions as mere words: they do not tell how sensation or life arises; they are placeholders for ignorance, not explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid making powers their own causes (will as cause of willing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Asserting that the faculty (capacity) to will is the cause of a particular act of willing is circular and uninformative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between general capacities (voluntas) and particular causation of acts; analysis should explain antecedent causes of specific volitions, not simply posit a generic faculty as cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not hide ignorance behind 'occult' causes
rubrics_metrics.description: Invoking 'fortune', 'ocult qualities', 'sympathy', 'antipathy', 'antiperistasis' and similar terms as causes merely disguises ignorance and substitutes empty labels for real agents or mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are names for unknown causes; good philosophy seeks discoverable agents or operations rather than resorting to mysterious-sounding placeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid inconsistent causal accounts in moral and civil philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: It is absurd to say God is the prime cause of law and of all actions but not the cause of injustice; such inconsistent attributions produce philosophical incoherence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demands consistent causal accounts: if God is claimed as cause of laws and actions, one must explain how moral deviation (injustice) arises without incoherent double-roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public good measured by law, not private appetite
rubrics_metrics.description: In civil society Good and Evil are determined not by private appetites but by the Law — the will and appetite of the State as public representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private passions as moral measure lead to disorder and subversion of commonwealth; monks/friars who judge by private vow exemplify the danger of substituting personal measures for public law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lawful marriage is not unchastity
rubrics_metrics.description: It is false to claim that the lawful work of marriage is repugnant to chastity or continence; such claims have been used to justify clerical celibacy for institutional gain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hobbes argues clerical prohibition of marriage followed institutional motives (popes/priests seeking heirs and wealth) rather than genuine moral necessity; warns against labeling natural duties sinful to achieve clerical advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not equate non-popular government with tyranny on name alone
rubrics_metrics.description: Calling all governments except popular ones 'tyranny' (and all kings 'tyrants') is a rhetorical abuse arising from popular resentment rather than reasoned judgement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hobbes explains that names acquire odious force through political conflict; proper political analysis should judge forms by their effects, not pejorative labels born of factional hatred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critique of 'Not Men, But Law Governs' (Aristotelian error)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aristotle's claim that in a well-ordered commonwealth men should not govern but the Laws is considered an error by Hobbes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicates that excessive abstraction about law governing independently of human enforcement neglects the realities of power, force, and enforcement that make law effective; warns that legalistic abstractions can mislead about governance.
